evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person request from a team member, not a spec. It has no numbered or bulleted acceptance list, no shall/must table and no feature matrix. Line 1 opens: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' The behaviour asks are user needs written in prose: line 3 'I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none, and I need to be able to undo my last move'; line 5 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor'; line 7 'If a message arrives while I am reading further up, leave my place alone and just tell me there is something new'. It does not turn into a build recipe. Line 11 says 'layout and names are yours'. Line 13 says 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', and it names only one route, GET /api/health. Line 13 does give the runtime contract (Node.js/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, /app/app.db/DB_PATH, seed path). Check 4 requires those facts, and the paragraph uses a conversational register ('Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages'). Lines 15-17 (seed loading, password, account list) are the expected house-convention facts that the skill lists as known false positives. There is no framework scaffold, file layout or endpoint list beyond the health check. The detailed rules live in /instructions/hireops_rules.md, which the brief cites as the team's own rules note (line 11). That note does use tables and bullets, but the skill's format puts runtime and rule detail in notes (check 4 wording 'in instruction.md or its /instructions notes'). Its naturalness is check 2's concern (voice consistency between brief and notes), not this row's verdict on the prompt. Broken-app / conforming-alternative probe: this is a prose-only row, so no app can pass or fail it. The relevant counter-test is whether a reader could take the brief as a dictated implementation. It cannot, because the brief explicitly hands over routes, file layout, names and page layout ('layout and names are yours', 'your call'). Runtime or judge evidence cannot bear on this row, so its absence leaves no measurement gap. The raw-evidence index was not needed for this verdict.
